intent: The heading that gives its Popover's panel its accessible name.
typical_uses: The one heading of a popover, stating what its controls set

dont_use_when.situation: The heading of a dialog's popup
The heading of a card on the page

invariants.text: PopoverTitle renders an h2 unless `render` replaces it; popover.module.css sets only its font weight, to the label weight, so the browser's own heading size and margins still apply.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a second PopoverTitle in the same popup
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep one PopoverTitle per popover and use plain headings for any subheadings; the popup's `aria-labelledby` points at one title's id

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the title's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the title's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through popover.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A title rendered as a third-level heading

bad.title: A plain heading in place of PopoverTitle
bad.why: A plain heading carries no id the primitive knows about, so the popup gets no `aria-labelledby` and a screen reader announces an unnamed dialog.

cannot_extract: heritage: "BaseUIComponentProps<'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'h5' | 'h6', PopoverTitleState>" admits 6 host elements (h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6); the contract names "h2", the element the declaring file documents the component as rendering - a caller may render another
